documents.title: Press Release - CPCL Financial Performance For The Quarter And Half Year Ended 30.09.2026
Announcement under Regulation 30 (LODR)-Press Release / Media Release

analysis.summary: Chennai Petroleum Corporation Limited (CPCL) reported a highest ever crude throughput of 11.71 MMT (112% of installed capacity) for FY 2025-26 and 2.93 MMT (111% of installed capacity) for Q4 FY26. Full-year gross refining margin (GRM) reached $9.2 per barrel compared to the Singapore benchmark of $5.83 per barrel, while Q4 GRM stood at $13.75 per barrel. The company reduced its debt-to-equity ratio at a gross level to 0.18 and recommended a record total dividend of INR 62 per share for the year. CPCL is expanding its capital outlay with INR 2,000 crores earmarked over the next 2 to 3 years for Group 2/3 LOBS and retail outlet projects. Chennai Petroleum Corporation Limited (CPCL) reported a crude throughput of 10.45 MMT for FY 2024-25, representing 99.5% of its installed capacity, with Q4 throughput reaching 113% of capacity.

guidance.claim: The company expects annual normal maintenance capex of approximately INR 500 crores.
guidance.quote: Besides, every year, you can assume another INR500 crores is our normal capex.

guidance.claim: CPCL expects maintenance CAPEX to be in the range of Rs. 200-250 crore for the next year.
guidance.quote: The maintenance CAPEX will be at around Rs. 200-250 crore range and depending on value added projects approvals, the actual will be a little different.

guidance.claim: Normal maintenance CAPEX for the next two years is projected at around Rs. 250 to Rs. 300 crores annually.
guidance.quote: The normal maintenance CAPEX for the next two years would be around Rs. 250 to Rs. 300 crores, maintenance CAPEX plus small regular CAPEX normally.

guidance.claim: If the LOBS project is approved, annual CAPEX for the next two years would increase to about Rs. 700 to Rs. 800 crores per year.
guidance.quote: With this project, about Rs. 700 to Rs. 800 crores per year.

demand_outlook.claim: CPCL's net GRM based on realized RTP is currently close to the long-term average.
demand_outlook.quote: The net GRM based on realized RTP is pretty close to the long-term average.

demand_outlook.claim: There is a clear shortfall of MS in the southern market of close to about 20 TMT per month where production is less than demand.
demand_outlook.quote: MS in southern market, there is a clear shortfall so, the production is less than demand. It is close to about 20 TMT per month.

demand_outlook.claim: Southern market growth forecast is around 4%-5% for MS and 3% for HSD.
demand_outlook.quote: Like MS, they are projecting 6% and here we see around 4%-5%. HSD we see at 3% growth forecast, as against 2.5% odd here.

capex_expansion.claim: CPCL incurred capex of INR 856 crores in FY 2025-26 compared to INR 673 crores in the previous year.
capex_expansion.quote: During the current year, the capex was INR856 crores as compared to INR673 crores in the previous year.

capex_expansion.claim: The Group 2 and Group 3 LOBS project carries a total project outlay of INR 1,600 crores.
capex_expansion.quote: LOBS project, Group 2, Group 3 LOBS project is INR1,600 crores.

capex_expansion.claim: CPCL's retail outlet endeavor has a planned outlay of INR 400 crores.
capex_expansion.quote: The retail outlet project is INR400 crores.

capex_expansion.claim: The new LOBS project will add 250 KTPA of fresh capacity in Group 2 and Group 3 grades.
capex_expansion.quote: My new unit will take me to a 250,000, 250 KTPA in Group 2, Group 3 capacity, and that will be a fresh addition.

capex_expansion.claim: CPCL incurred CAPEX of Rs. 673 crores during FY 2024-25.
capex_expansion.quote: On the CAPEX front, in the current year, we have spent Rs. 673 crores as CAPEX for the current year.

capex_expansion.claim: The revised capital cost for the Cauvery Basin Refinery project is Rs. 36,354 crores with a 25:75 equity holding between CPCL and Indian Oil.
capex_expansion.quote: The revised capital cost is at Rs. 36,354 crores with a 25:75 equity holding between CPCL and Indian oil respectively.

capex_expansion.claim: CPCL has full custody of 1,200 acres of land for the Cauvery Basin Refinery project.
capex_expansion.quote: The most important updates with respect to the project is now we have full custody of the land. So, about 600 acres, which was already with CPCL and another 600 acres, which was acquired in the process, both is in our possession and the pre-project activities of boundary wall construction, and all those things are almost at a big stage.

capex_expansion.claim: CPCL introduced pharma-grade hexane during the year, expanding its value-added product range.
capex_expansion.quote: Pharma-grade hexane is a new product that we introduced during the year which gives us inroads into a new market altogether.

capex_expansion.claim: CPCL plans an additional 1.5 MW floating solar power installation.

margins_costs.claim: Q4 FY26 GRM reached $13.75 per barrel against the Singapore benchmark of $8.70 per barrel.
margins_costs.quote: The GRM for quarter 4 was $13.75 barrel as compared to Singapore benchmark of $8.70 per barrel, which again reiterates that all these efficiencies are constant, continuous and are being sustained over each period.

margins_costs.claim: CPCL's core GRM for Q4 FY26 was $10.3 per barrel.
CPCL processed 52% high sulphur crude during the financial year.
margins_costs.quote: During the financial year, we processed 52% high sulphur.

margins_costs.claim: Full-year GRM for FY 2024-25 stood at $4.22 per barrel compared to $8.64 per barrel in FY 2023-24.
margins_costs.quote: The GRM for 2024-25 for a full year basis is $4.22 per barrel as compared to the previous year $8.64 per barrel, but if you compare it to Singapore benchmark which was $3.79 per barrel in the current year, we have performed better.

margins_costs.claim: CPCL recorded a GRM of $6.22 per barrel in Q4 FY 2024-25 against the Singapore benchmark of $3.1 per barrel.
margins_costs.quote: On Quarter 4, our GRM was $6.22 per barrel. Again, if I compare the previous year same quarter, it was $7.7 per barrel, but if I compare it to Singapore benchmark, which was only $3.1 per barrel.

margins_costs.claim: Fuel and loss reduced to 8.51% for the full year FY 2024-25.
margins_costs.quote: and in that context, the fuel and loss has come down to 8.51% for the year as a whole.

margins_costs.claim: Inventory gain for Q4 FY 2024-25 was $0.66 per barrel, amounting to Rs. 125 crores.
margins_costs.quote: Yes, the inventory gain is not very significant for the quarter. It is only $ 0.66 per barrel. And in absolute rupee terms, it is Rs. 125 crores only.

margins_costs.claim: Average discount on opportunity crude for FY 2024-25 was around $1.5-$2 per barrel.
margins_costs.quote: Last year, that is the Financial Year’24-25, the average was around $1.5-$2.

margins_costs.claim: CPCL reported a gross refining margin of $3.40 per barrel for 9M FY2024-25.
Net operating expenditure stood at Rs 945 crore for 9M FY2024-25.

orders_capacity.claim: CPCL registered its highest ever crude throughput of 11.71 MMT in FY 2025-26, operating at 112% of installed capacity.
orders_capacity.quote: CPCL achieved a highest ever crude throughput of 11.71 MMT, million metric ton, which equivalents to 112% of installed capacity, breaking records of our previous best of 11.64 MMT achieved in financial year 2023-'24.

orders_capacity.claim: Crude throughput for Q4 FY26 reached 2.93 MMT, translating to 111% of installed capacity.
orders_capacity.quote: In quarter 4 of the current financial year, CPCL achieved a crude throughput of 2.93 MMT, which is also 111% of installed capacity.

orders_capacity.claim: The company achieved highest ever annual production of 5.139 MMT for diesel (HSD) and 1.318 MMT for petrol (MS).
orders_capacity.quote: CPCL concluded the financial year on a high note, achieving the highest ever production levels of 5.139 MMT for diesel HSD, and 1.318 MMT of petrol that is MS, an impressive testament of the refinery's outstanding operational performance.

orders_capacity.claim: Distillate yield reached a record high of 79.1% during the financial year.
orders_capacity.quote: Further, highest ever distillate yield of 79.1%, beating our previous record of 77.6% set in 2019-'20 was also achieved during this year.

orders_capacity.claim: CPCL registered crude throughput of 10.45 MMT in FY 2024-25, achieving 99.5% capacity utilization.
orders_capacity.quote: CPCL achieved a crude throughput of 10.45 MMT, equivalent to 99.5% of our installed capacity and this must be seen with respect to the turnaround that has happened during the year

orders_capacity.claim: Crude throughput reached 2.974 MMT in Q4 FY 2024-25, representing 113% of installed capacity.
orders_capacity.quote: and coming on to Quarter 4, the crude throughput was 2.974, which is 113% of installed capacity.

orders_capacity.claim: CPCL processed 64% - 65% high sulfur crude during FY 2024-25.
orders_capacity.quote: During the financial year, we have processed almost 64% - 65% of high sulfur.

orders_capacity.claim: CPCL processed crude throughput of 7,480 TMT during 9M FY2024-25.
CPCL's installed solar power capacity stands at 2.5 MW.

capital_allocation.claim: CPCL's gross debt to equity ratio improved to 0.18 compared to 0.39 in the previous year.
capital_allocation.quote: Our leverage position now stands at 0.18. Our debt equity stands at 0.18 at a gross level as compared to 0.39 last year.

capital_allocation.claim: Gross borrowings stand at INR 1,900 crores, while net borrowings are INR 973 crores with a net debt ratio of 0.09.
capital_allocation.quote: On a gross basis, the borrowings are INR1,900 crores, but on a net basis, it is less than INR1,000 crores, to be precise, INR973 crores.

capital_allocation.claim: CPCL recommended a total dividend of INR 62 per share for FY 2025-26, comprising an interim dividend of INR 8 and a final dividend of INR 54 per share.
capital_allocation.quote: During the year, for the first time, CPCL paid an interim dividend, and we are happy to announce that in addition to the interim dividend of INR8 per equity share of INR10 each, the Board has recommended a final dividend of INR54 per share, taking the total dividend for the year to INR62 per share, which again is highest ever.

capital_allocation.claim: Debt to equity ratio stood at 0.39 as on March 31, 2025, with total debt at Rs. 3,100 crores.
capital_allocation.quote: When I turn to leverage position, the debt equity position as on March 31, 2025, is 0.39 compared to 0.32 in the previous year. At an absolute level, the debt stands at Rs. 3,100 crores as compared to Rs. 2,762 crores as on March 31, 2024.

capital_allocation.claim: Net worth of CPCL stood at Rs. 7,939 crores as on March 31, 2025.
capital_allocation.quote: Net worth is at Rs. 7,939 crores as on March 31, 2025.

capital_allocation.claim: The Board recommended a dividend of Rs. 5 per equity share for FY 2024-25.
capital_allocation.quote: With the above, the Board has also recommended a dividend of Rs. 5 per equity share that is 50% of face value for the current year and as we all know, this is subject to approval at AGM, which will happen in the due course.

capital_allocation.claim: CPCL is currently working with a 2:1 debt equity structure for the new Cauvery Basin Refinery joint venture.
capital_allocation.quote: Presently, we are working with a 2:1 debt equity for this JV.

capital_allocation.claim: CPCL's net worth stood at Rs 7,491 crore as of December 2024.

risks_headwinds.claim: Foreign exchange losses amounted to approximately INR 200 crores for Q4 and INR 350 crores for the full year.
risks_headwinds.quote: For the quarter, it would be for the quarter, it is approximately INR 200 crores,. And for the whole year, it will be around INR350 crores.

risks_headwinds.claim: Short-term supply disturbances affected 30% to 40% of Middle East crude shipments over a brief period.
risks_headwinds.quote: What has impacted is that maybe 30% to 40% was affected over a very short period, but all have assured us that depending on the situation, they will make up all the cargoes.

risks_headwinds.claim: Lower international product cracks impacted profitability as HSD cracks declined from $13-$15 per barrel to sub-10 levels.
risks_headwinds.quote: The primary reason is the international cracks. The cracks which were there at about close to $13 to $15 per barrel in HSD and other products has come down to 10 or sub- 10 level in the current year.

risks_headwinds.claim: For the full year FY 2024-25, inventory registered a loss of $0.06 per barrel, amounting to Rs. 40 crores.
risks_headwinds.quote: But on an overall annual basis, the inventory would be a loss that is $ 0.06 per barrel, Rs. 40 crores in amount.

risks_headwinds.claim: CPCL incurred CST under-recovery of Rs 246 crore during 9M FY2024-25.
CPCL reported an exchange variation loss of Rs 122 crore for 9M FY2024-25.

management_commitments.claim: CPCL expects commissioning of several retail outlets to take place during FY 2026-27.
management_commitments.quote: And this year, that is '26-'27, we'll see a lot of commissioning out of them.

management_commitments.claim: CPCL plans to incur INR 2,000 crores on its LOBS and retail outlet projects over a period of 2 to 3 years.
management_commitments.quote: This INR2,000 crores will happen over 2 to 3 years.

management_commitments.claim: CPCL expects maintenance CAPEX to be around Rs. 200-250 crore range for the next year.
management_commitments.quote: The maintenance CAPEX will be at around Rs. 200-250 crore range and depending on value added projects approvals, the actual will be a little different.

management_commitments.claim: CPCL expects normal maintenance CAPEX to be around Rs. 250 to Rs. 300 crores annually for the next two years.
management_commitments.quote: The normal maintenance CAPEX for the next two years would be around Rs. 250 to Rs. 300 crores, maintenance CAPEX plus small regular CAPEX normally.

management_commitments.claim: Refinery crude unit 1 catering to lubes will undergo scheduled maintenance around August-September 2025.
management_commitments.quote: In 2025, our refinery crude unit 1 which caters to lubes will go into maintenance around August, September.

_meta.note: Facts are verbatim-grounded against the company's own documents; claims whose quote was not found were dropped.
